title: God in nature
hookLine: Nanak says he is a sacrifice to the One who dwells in creation (Asa di Var, ang 469)

lines: BALIHARI: I'D GIVE MYSELF FOR YOU.
ASA DI VAR, IN THE EARLY MORNING.
NOT PAST THE CLOUDS. RIGHT HERE.
cards: Balihari. It's a word of love so strong it borrows the language of offering: I am a sacrifice to you, I'd give myself for you. In Punjabi homes it can be said over a child.
In the Granth it's said to God. And in one line of Asa di Var, the hymn sung in the early morning, Guru Nanak says where he finds the One he'd give himself for. Not in a temple.
Not up past the clouds. Right here, in the made world, in the stuff of a walk outside.

teach.h: ANG 469: A SACRIFICE TO YOU IN CREATION.
teach.b: First, the line, at Ang four hundred sixty-nine. In paraphrase: I am a sacrifice to You, who dwell in Your creation; Your limit cannot be known.
The word for creation is kudrat: nature, the made world, and also the power that makes it. The One isn't parked somewhere outside it, looking in. Second, what kudrat holds.
Earlier in Asa di Var, in a salok, Guru Nanak runs through it.

teach.h: KUDRAT: EARTH, SKY, AIR, WATER, FIRE.
teach.b: In paraphrase: by Your power we see, by Your power we hear; Yours are the earth and the skies, the air and the water and the fire, the creatures of every kind, even fear and comfort.
It reads like someone standing outdoors, turning slowly, naming. Third, in, not equal to. The same line says the One's limit can't be known.
The Creator dwells in creation and isn't used up by it. A field at dawn is not the whole of God, but nothing in it is empty of God either. Fourth, an ordinary walk.

teach.h: A PIGEON ON A WIRE IS A PLACE TO LOOK.
teach.b: If the One dwells in the made world, then a pigeon on a wire, a weed in a sidewalk crack, rain running down a window are not background.
They're places to look. And Guru Nanak's answer to seeing them isn't a theory. It's balihari: love so full it wants to give itself.

how: Asa di Var is sung in gurdwaras in the early morning; Sikhs read its lines on kudrat as saying the Creator dwells in creation while remaining beyond it.

o: a hymn sung only in the open air at dawn
the One dwelling in the made world, and beyond it
a rule to pray outdoors rather than indoors

games.q: God in nature: tap the pairs.
p: I am a sacrifice to you
creation, and the power that makes it

s: the Granth says a tree is God
the Creator dwells in creation and is also beyond it.
Guru Nanak lists earth, sky, air, water and fire as God's kudrat
in a salok of Asa di Var.
Guru Nanak places God only beyond the clouds
he offers himself to the One who dwells in creation.

games.q: you want to find the One Guru Nanak loves. where does the line at Ang 469 point you?
o: into the made world, the creation itself.
away from the world, past the clouds.
games.why: he's a sacrifice to the One who dwells in kudrat, whose limit cannot be known.

practice: If you can, step outside or stand at a window, and let your eyes rest on one living thing: a tree, a patch of grass, a bird, a cloud moving. Don't name it or judge it; just look, the way Guru Nanak turns slowly and lists.
If your mind drifts, come back to the one thing.

wordCard.voice: God in nature. In Asa di Var, Guru Nanak offers himself to the One who dwells in kudrat, the made world, and whose limit cannot be known. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: kudrat, creation, nature, and the creative power behind it.

carryVoice: Your line: he dwells in nature. Nothing in the made world is empty of the One. See you tomorrow.
